standard_prerequisites.name: Stalks of a sheaf of modules and the localization maps along specializations: for a specialization x' in the closure of {x} the stalk at x' of a module sheaf receives the stalk at x by localization at a multiplicative set
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof lines 669-671, where F_{x'} is identified as a localization of the module F_x
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the reduction of the statement to the vanishing of a localization of a zero module.

standard_prerequisites.name: The support of F is the set of points with nonzero stalk, so its complement is the locus where the stalk vanishes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at statement line 663 and proof line 671
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the conclusion 'closed under specialization' into the equivalent statement that the complement is closed under generalization.

core_obligations: Reduce to stalks: let x' be a specialization of a point x with F_x = 0, and prove that the stalk at x' vanishes (proof lines 668-669).
Use that the stalk at the specialization is a localization of the module F_x, so that it is zero whenever F_x is zero (proof lines 669-671).
Conclude that the complement of the support is closed under generalization, which is the stated closedness of the support under specialization (proof lines 671-672).
proof_roadmap: Argue on stalks along a specialization: a vanishing stalk at the generization forces a vanishing stalk at the specialization, because stalk maps are localizations (proof lines 667-672).
difficulty_reason: The statement is that for a quasi-coherent sheaf F on a scheme X the support is closed under specialization (statement lines 660-665). The counted proof is two lines long and its whole content is the observation that for a specialization x' of x the stalk of F at x' is a localization of the stalk at x, so the vanishing of F_x forces the vanishing of F_{x'}; the conclusion is then restated as closedness of the complement under generalization (proof lines 667-672). It is H2 by the rule that H3 is only given for genuinely independent research-level content: the argument is complete and uses no hypothesis beyond quasi-coherence being available for the notion of support, but it is a routine local argument and is deliberately not dressed up.
